rules.title: Template Similarity Detection
rules.description: The order of the page's sections matches the common AI-SaaS landing template: Hero, Feature grid, Logo cloud, Testimonials, Pricing, FAQ, Call-to-action band. Objective check: each section is classified from the page structure and the page's order is compared with the template order (longest common subsequence). 5 or more of the 7 in order fails; 4 needs a person.
rules.source: Avara editorial pattern (AI SaaS landing template); reference: NN/g Homepage Design Principles
rules.confidenceBasis: Admitted 2026-11-22 as documented Avara guidance: measurable pass/fail condition, failing and clean fixtures in test/score-admission.mjs (src/rules/_admissions.json). The cited source is a reference; its passage is not verified.
rules.evaluationPrompt: Template Similarity Detection: The order of the page's sections matches the common AI-SaaS landing template: Hero, Feature grid, Logo cloud, Testimonials, Pricing, FAQ, Call-to-action band. Objective check: each section is classified from the page structure and the page's order is compared with the template order (longest common subsequence). 5 or more of the 7 in order fails; 4 needs a person. Deterministic evidence first; a person confirms. A model does not decide this rule.
rules.recommendationTemplate: Your landing page follows the section order {{observation}} Change the order or replace at least two of these sections with content only you can show (a real product walkthrough, a customer's numbers, a comparison). Sections found: {{evidence}}
rules.userImpact: Visitors who have seen the same layout elsewhere read the page as generic before they read the words. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
rules.businessImpact: A page that looks like any other template makes the product feel interchangeable, which weakens the reason to choose it over alternatives. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
requiredEvidence: classified section list in page order

rules.title: Visual Distinctiveness
rules.description: The visual style departs from the default look. Objective check: count four default-style signals: a default sans font as the main typeface, a violet or indigo primary colour (hue 235 to 290), gradient backgrounds or gradient text, and rounded corners of 12px or more on cards. 3 or 4 signals needs a person.
rules.source: Refactoring UI; Material Design colour guidance
rules.evaluationPrompt: Visual Distinctiveness: The visual style departs from the default look. Objective check: count four default-style signals: a default sans font as the main typeface, a violet or indigo primary colour (hue 235 to 290), gradient backgrounds or gradient text, and rounded corners of 12px or more on cards. 3 or 4 signals needs a person. Deterministic evidence first; a person confirms. A model does not decide this rule.
rules.recommendationTemplate: The page uses {{observation}} together, which is the default look of many generated sites. Pick one choice that is yours (a typeface, a colour that is not violet, a distinctive shape or illustration style) and apply it consistently. Evidence: {{evidence}}
rules.userImpact: Visitors cannot tell this product from others by sight, so nothing about the page is remembered. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
rules.businessImpact: Default styling makes the brand forgettable and price the main difference. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
requiredEvidence: main font and share of text

heroLayout.note: Avara DIFF-002 detector pack: geometric comparison of the first-screen hero (heading, main action, lead visual) with a versioned, permissioned reference set at the same viewport. Diagnostic only: stored per scan, never shown as an observation or scored until a person approves a release policy from held-out real-site validation. DIFF-001 owns section order.

rules.title: Brand Memorability
rules.description: The page carries identifiable brand assets. Objective check: count four gaps: no logo mark (image or SVG) in the header, no favicon, no imagery beyond small icons, and a generic page title (Home, Welcome, Untitled). 3 or more needs a person.
rules.evaluationPrompt: Brand Memorability: The page carries identifiable brand assets. Objective check: count four gaps: no logo mark (image or SVG) in the header, no favicon, no imagery beyond small icons, and a generic page title (Home, Welcome, Untitled). 3 or more needs a person. Deterministic evidence first; a person confirms. A model does not decide this rule.
rules.recommendationTemplate: The page lacks {{observation}}. Add at least two assets that are recognisably yours: a logo mark, a favicon, a signature image or illustration, and a title that names the product and what it does. Evidence: {{evidence}}
rules.userImpact: With no recognisable assets there is little for a visitor to remember or recognise on return. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
rules.businessImpact: Low recall makes repeat visits and word of mouth harder. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.

rules.title: Dashboard Sameness
rules.description: A public app or dashboard view follows the stock dashboard layout. Objective check: look for a left sidebar of 5 or more links, a row of 3 or more small stat cards (number, label, change), and a chart card. All three present fails; two needs a person; a page with no app UI is not applicable.
rules.source: Material Design; Apple Human Interface Guidelines
rules.evaluationPrompt: Dashboard Sameness: A public app or dashboard view follows the stock dashboard layout. Objective check: look for a left sidebar of 5 or more links, a row of 3 or more small stat cards (number, label, change), and a chart card. All three present fails; two needs a person; a page with no app UI is not applicable. Deterministic evidence first; a person confirms. A model does not decide this rule.
rules.recommendationTemplate: The dashboard uses {{observation}}, the stock analytics layout. Organise the first screen around the one decision your user makes there, and show that decision's data first. Evidence: {{evidence}}
rules.userImpact: Users get no cue about what matters most, so they scan everything equally. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
rules.businessImpact: A dashboard that looks like every other gives no visible reason to prefer this product's insight. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.

rules.title: Layout Originality
rules.description: Sections use more than the three stock layouts. Objective check: classify each section as centred stack, 3-column grid or 2-column split and count the distinct layouts. With 5 or more sections and at most 2 distinct layouts it needs a person.
rules.evaluationPrompt: Layout Originality: Sections use more than the three stock layouts. Objective check: classify each section as centred stack, 3-column grid or 2-column split and count the distinct layouts. With 5 or more sections and at most 2 distinct layouts it needs a person. Deterministic evidence first; a person confirms. A model does not decide this rule.
rules.recommendationTemplate: Nearly every section uses {{observation}}. Change the layout of at least two sections to fit their content (a wide comparison, a timeline, an annotated screenshot). Evidence: {{evidence}}
rules.userImpact: Identical layouts make sections blur together, so visitors skim past them. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
rules.businessImpact: Uniform pages look templated and make the product feel generic. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.

rules.title: Visual System Originality
rules.description: The shape and icon language is chosen, not default. Objective check: three signals: every card shares one radius of 12px or more, most cards carry the same soft shadow, and icons come from a stock outline set (24px viewBox, 2px stroke) or are emoji. 2 or 3 signals needs a person.
rules.source: Refactoring UI; Apple Human Interface Guidelines
rules.evaluationPrompt: Visual System Originality: The shape and icon language is chosen, not default. Objective check: three signals: every card shares one radius of 12px or more, most cards carry the same soft shadow, and icons come from a stock outline set (24px viewBox, 2px stroke) or are emoji. 2 or 3 signals needs a person. Deterministic evidence first; a person confirms. A model does not decide this rule.
rules.recommendationTemplate: The page uses {{observation}}, the default shape and icon language. Choose one shape rule of your own (square corners, heavy borders, a distinct illustration set) and use it throughout. Evidence: {{evidence}}
rules.userImpact: A default visual language gives visitors no cue that this product has a point of view. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
rules.businessImpact: Visual sameness lowers recall and perceived craft. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
requiredEvidence: share of cards with a shadow
icon count and how many match a stock set

rules.title: Information Hierarchy Differentiation
rules.description: Sections do not all share one structure. Objective check: fingerprint each section by alignment, supporting text, call to action, media and card group; if 80% or more of 5 or more sections share one fingerprint, the page has a flat, repeating rhythm and needs a person.
rules.evaluationPrompt: Information Hierarchy Differentiation: Sections do not all share one structure. Objective check: fingerprint each section by alignment, supporting text, call to action, media and card group; if 80% or more of 5 or more sections share one fingerprint, the page has a flat, repeating rhythm and needs a person. Deterministic evidence first; a person confirms. A model does not decide this rule.
rules.recommendationTemplate: {{observation}} Vary the emphasis: make the one section that matters most larger or different in kind, and shorten the rest. Evidence: {{evidence}}
rules.userImpact: When every section is presented the same way, nothing signals what to read first. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
rules.businessImpact: A flat hierarchy hides the strongest argument for the product. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
requiredEvidence: share using the most common fingerprint

rules.title: Trust Through Design
rules.description: Proof is built so a visitor can check it. Objective check: flag the generic trust band: a logo row where none of the logos link anywhere, and testimonial cards with quote marks or stars but no link to a source or case study. Both present needs a person.
rules.source: NN/g Trustworthiness in Web Design; Baymard perceived security
rules.evaluationPrompt: Trust Through Design: Proof is built so a visitor can check it. Objective check: flag the generic trust band: a logo row where none of the logos link anywhere, and testimonial cards with quote marks or stars but no link to a source or case study. Both present needs a person. Deterministic evidence first; a person confirms. A model does not decide this rule.
rules.recommendationTemplate: The trust section is {{observation}}. Make at least one proof checkable: link logos to case studies, name the person and company on each quote, or show a number with its source. Evidence: {{evidence}}
rules.userImpact: Logos and quotes that cannot be checked read as decoration, so they add little confidence. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
rules.businessImpact: Unverifiable proof gives up the main chance to reduce purchase risk. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
requiredEvidence: logo count and how many link
testimonial cards and how many link

rules.title: Feature Grid Saturation
rules.description: The page is not mostly grids of same-looking icon cards. Objective check: count grids of 3 or more cards, each with an icon, heading and short text. 2 or more such grids need a person (a count of grids is a pattern, never a confirmed failure); one passes.
rules.source: NN/g Ten Usability Heuristics (aesthetic and minimalist design)
rules.evaluationPrompt: Feature Grid Saturation: The page is not mostly grids of same-looking icon cards. Objective check: count grids of 3 or more cards, each with an icon, heading and short text. 2 or more such grids need a person (a count of grids is a pattern, never a confirmed failure); one passes. Deterministic evidence first; a person confirms. A model does not decide this rule.
rules.recommendationTemplate: The page has {{observation}}. Keep the grid for the features that matter most and show the rest differently: one annotated screenshot, a short list, or a worked example. Evidence: {{evidence}}
rules.userImpact: Repeated icon cards are scanned, not read, and make features blur into one another. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
rules.businessImpact: Feature grids that look the same as competitors' do not show why this product is better. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
requiredEvidence: each grid: selector, card count, card titles

rules.title: Visual Commodity Risk
rules.description: Summary of how many independent sameness signals were flagged. It adds no deduction, no score and no finding of its own. Patterns are recorded in Pattern Intelligence once enough pages exist.
rules.source: Avara rollup of DIFF-001 to DIFF-009
rules.evaluationPrompt: Visual Commodity Risk: Summary of how many independent sameness signals were flagged. It adds no deduction, no score and no finding of its own. Patterns are recorded in Pattern Intelligence once enough pages exist. Deterministic evidence first; a person confirms. A model does not decide this rule.
rules.userImpact: See the findings it summarises. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
rules.businessImpact: See the findings it summarises. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.

rules.title: Owner-Specified Brand Cues Present
rules.description: Check whether the brand cues the owner named (logo, colour, character, phrase) appear in the first screen. Without owner-supplied cues the result is insufficient evidence. Memorability needs audience research; a screenshot cannot establish it.
rules.evaluationPrompt: Check whether the brand cues the owner named (logo, colour, character, phrase) appear in the first screen. Without owner-supplied cues the result is insufficient evidence. Memorability needs audience research; a screenshot cannot establish it. Ground every point in an exact quote, a screenshot region or a browser measurement from the context. If the context does not show it, answer insufficient evidence.
rules.recommendationTemplate: Show the brand cue you named in the first screen: {{observation}}

criterion.applicability: Scans where the owner supplied brand cues.
exceptions: No owner cues: insufficient evidence, never unmet.
Recognition and memorability require audience evidence.

supplementary.name: Ehrenberg-Bass, Building Distinctive Brand Assets (book listing)

rules.userImpact: Visitors may not connect the page with the brand they know.
rules.businessImpact: Brand cues may be missed. This is a hypothesis; recognition needs audience research.
requiredEvidence: an exact quote from the page

rules.title: A Specific Differentiator Is Stated
rules.description: Check whether the page states at least one concrete, checkable way it differs (a number, a named method, a named audience) rather than generic claims. Quote it, or quote the generic claim.
rules.sourceSection: Principle 2: Communicate Who You Are and What You Do
rules.evaluationPrompt: Check whether the page states at least one concrete, checkable way it differs (a number, a named method, a named audience) rather than generic claims. Quote it, or quote the generic claim. Ground every point in an exact quote, a screenshot region or a browser measurement from the context. If the context does not show it, answer insufficient evidence.
rules.recommendationTemplate: State one concrete, checkable way you differ: {{observation}}

criterion.section: Principle 2: Communicate Who You Are and What You Do
exceptions: A portfolio differentiates through its work samples; quoting a project counts.

rules.userImpact: Visitors comparing options cannot see why to choose you.
rules.businessImpact: The page may read like its competitors. This is a hypothesis; Avara did not measure choice.
requiredEvidence: an exact quote from the page
